summary: Redwood team walked Atlas Finance through a migration demo focusing on feature parity across OpenAI/Anthropic/Together -> Redwood API. Discussed parameter mappings (temperature/top_p/max_tokens), streaming and function calling support, embeddings parity, and operational differences between hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. Security and compliance (SOC2, KMS, audit logs, SSO) were key asks. Agreed next steps to share parity mapping + pricing and to kick off a POC within ~30-45 days.
transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-03-31 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Sam Ortiz (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Atlas CTO), Maya Patel (Atlas ML Eng), Chris Rivera (Atlas Security), Samir Gupta (Atlas SRE)

[00:00] Alex Kim: hey everyone thanks for joining, um gonna run through a migration demo today, we'll map parity from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together into Redwood's API, and then Priya will jump into the console and optimize suggestions.
[00:28] Jordan Lee: great thanks Alex, quick note, we have tight latency SLOs for prod, also security is a blocking item.
[00:45] Alex Kim: totally, and we'll cover dedicated vs hosted, and our private options. Priya do you want to start with the API parity?
[01:08] Priya Desai: yeah sure, so first, basic request mapping: max_tokens, temperature, top_p, stop sequences map 1:1 to Redwood "max_tokens", "temp", "top_p". streaming is supported via SSE streaming endpoint, function-calling is supported but we call them "tools" in our SDK — small naming difference.
[01:45] Maya Patel: when you say tools, is that compatible with the current OpenAI function-calling framing? we rely on the structured return for downstream parsers.
[02:02] Priya Desai: yes, we have structured output and schema enforcement. sometimes the auto-transcription will say schema as "structure", but functionally it's the same, the response payload includes a tools array and you can configure sync or async execution.
[02:30] Sam Ortiz: just to add, embeddings endpoint maps straightforwardly — provide the model name (we surface open models and our verified profiles). vector dimension parity depends on model family; we'll show mapping table.
[02:57] Jordan Lee: mapping table would be great. And cost — we've looked at perf vs cost and need guidance at scale.
[03:12] Alex Kim: yes, we'll include a cost estimate example; the parity doc will show token math plus suggested batching and caching to reduce unit cost.
[03:35] Chris Rivera: security questions up front — KMS? audit logs? where's data stored for hosted?
[03:48] Priya Desai: hosted keeps minimal transient data, but for enterprise we offer Dedicated and Private (VPC/on-prem) with customer-managed KMS and full audit logs. SOC2 and ISO artifacts are in our security package which I'll share.
[04:20] Jordan Lee: great. can you run through a live request translation — like a TogetherAI prompt that we're using for summarization and then the Redwood equivalent?
[04:38] Priya Desai: yeah watch screen, I'll paste an example prompt and show the payload diff. (screen share) Here's a Together model call: model: together-small, prompt: ... top_p 0.9, temp 0.3, max_tokens 450, streaming true. In Redwood you'd use model: redwood-compat-together-small (we auto-route to optimized kernels), set temp=0.3, top_p=0.9, max_tokens=450, and enable streaming=true. The response formatting is same, but backend kernels may be quantized for cost.
[05:20] Maya Patel: Any differences in tokenization? we do subword token counts for billing and we need to reconcile totals.
[05:35] Priya Desai: good point — tokenization can vary; our parity sheet includes approximate token multipliers per model family. we recommend running a short tokenization pass during POC to calibrate billing.
[06:05] Samir Gupta: how about KV cache behavior for multi-turn chat? we use cached KV to maintain context; if migrating, do we need to rearchitect?
[06:20] Sam Ortiz: Redwood supports KV cache and automatic prefix caching; typical apps should see similar latency. if you use long context windows you'll benefit from our runtime kernels that optimize attention for longer sequences.
[06:45] Jordan Lee: latency — what numbers can you show on p50/p95 for these families?
[06:58] Priya Desai: we have benchmark profiles in the console. for redwood-compat-together-small on a Dedicated T4-like pool p50 ~70ms token, p95 ~230ms token for 2k contexts, but this varies by batch size and quantization. we'll attach the verified perf sheet.
[07:28] Maya Patel: those look promising. what about streaming semantics — do you support chunked events ala OpenAI streams?
[07:36] Priya Desai: yes SSE with chunked tokens similar to OpenAI, though field names differ slightly in the wire protocol; our SDKs handle that mapping.
[07:57] Chris Rivera: for compliance we need end-to-end encryption at rest, bring-your-own-key, and indelible audit logs. Can Redwood do BYOK?
[08:12] Alex Kim: yes, BYOK via KMS/HSM integrations for Dedicated and Private. hosted supports envelope encryption but enterprise buys Dedicated/Private for BYOK guarantees.
[08:34] Jordan Lee: ok, thanks. can you talk about fallback strategies — if our primary model is unavailable, do you auto-fallback to a cheaper model?
[08:48] Sam Ortiz: we support routing policies, canarying and automatic fallbacks to compatible model variants. you control policy: latency-first, cost-first, region-first.
[09:05] Maya Patel: on canaries — our release process needs A/B traffic split and automatic rollback on quality regressions. integrate with our eval suite?
[09:20] Priya Desai: Redwood Optimize ties to prompt sets/evals — you can configure regression alerts and automatic rollback thresholds. we can show an example in the console.
[09:45] Alex Kim: ok moving on, I'll share the parity mapping doc now, it's in the drive link in the chat. (link pasted)
[10:00] Jordan Lee: got it. seeing the mapping — question: Together uses a different sampling schedule for temperature in some models, is that handled?
[10:12] Priya Desai: sampling differences exist; our mapping flags models where behavior differs slightly. during POC we validate sample outputs and maybe apply small post-processing to align.
[10:32] Maya Patel: about embeddings — we're currently on OpenAI ada embeddings. do you have a drop-in mapping for embedding dims and similarity scoring?
[10:45] Sam Ortiz: yes we map dims and recommend similarity normalize factors. we'll include sample nearest-neighbor recall numbers from our benchmark.
[11:05] Jordan Lee: can you demo the console Optimize tab where you suggested batching and quantization?
[11:15] Priya Desai: sure, switching to console. (screen share) Here is the Optimize view; it shows per-route token cost, suggestions like dynamic batching, KV caching thresholds, and recommended quantization profile for the model.
[11:45] Maya Patel: the quantization recommendations — do they affect output quality? we need low regression risk.
[11:55] Priya Desai: we provide quality regression estimates tied to eval prompt sets. for critical routes we recommend conservative quant (e.g., int8) and A/B test before full rollout.
[12:20] Chris Rivera: on governance, do you provide role-based access for console and audit of who invoked what keys?
[12:30] Priya Desai: yes RBAC, SSO/SAML and full audit logs on Dedicated/Private. logs include token-level usage metadata (not payload) and API keys usage; we can extend retention for enterprise.
[12:55] Jordan Lee: any gotchas moving from streaming OpenAI to Redwood?
[13:05] Sam Ortiz: small wire-protocol differences, but Redwood's SDKs handle most conversions; we recommend a quick compatibility shim if you have bespoke stream handlers.
[13:30] Maya Patel: ok can you show an example of a function/tool call conversion — our orchestrator expects a JSON return with code blocks.
[13:45] Priya Desai: sure — here's an example payload (shared). the tools array includes name, args, and a status field. output formatting includes a content field with structured JSON — you can set the schema enforcement flag to ensure strict JSON.
[14:20] Jordan Lee: that's useful. does Redwood support user-defined tool endpoints that run in our infra?
[14:32] Alex Kim: we support webhook tool calls and for Private deployments you can host tools inside your network and call them securely.
[14:50] Maya Patel: what's the typical migration timeline? weeks? months?
[15:00] Alex Kim: simple apps can migrate in 2-4 weeks; large scale with dedicated capacity and compliance checks often 6-10 weeks including POC and security review. we recommend a 30-45 day POC to validate perf and quality.
[15:22] Samir Gupta: during POC what metrics should we collect?
[15:30] Priya Desai: token volumes, p50/p95 latency, error rates, average response size in tokens, RLHF rollout quality metrics if you use any, and cost per 1M tokens.
[15:48] Jordan Lee: ok, on costs — your matching shows some cost savings with batching, how conservative is that?
[16:00] Priya Desai: conservative — we model realistic burst and tail behavior, but we'll run benchmarks with your traffic to produce a more accurate estimate.
[16:18] Alex Kim: demo note: a few names may be slightly mis-transcribed in this call, but we'll attach original recording.
[16:30] Maya Patel: can we talk about model pinning and rollouts — we want to freeze a model for compliance but still get security patches.
[16:42] Priya Desai: you can pin model versions and we support security patching at the infra layer; we produce a changelog for any behavioral changes. for regulated customers we recommend Dedicated or Private so you control rollouts.
[17:05] Jordan Lee: what about data residency — our EU customers require EU-only hosting.
[17:15] Alex Kim: we have EU regions and Private deployments can be fully localized. we'll note region-specific deployment options in the follow-up.
[17:35] Chris Rivera: can you confirm logs don't contain PII?
[17:42] Priya Desai: logs are metadata-only by default, payloads are not stored for hosted unless explicitly enabled; for Dedicated/Private you control retention and masking.
[18:00] Sam Ortiz: switching back to parity mapping — here's the table: OpenAI gpt-4 -> redwood-compat-gpt4-ish, Anthropic claude -> redwood-compat-claude-style, Together -> redwood-compat-together-family. the compatibility is behavioral but we test on your evals.
[18:30] Maya Patel: how do we validate semantic equivalence? we have prompt suites.
[18:42] Priya Desai: Redwood Optimize runs evals against prompt suites and reports change in metrics (accuracy, hallucination rates, latency). we can run your suite during POC.
[19:05] Jordan Lee: are there any feature gaps e.g., OpenAI embeddings older releases had hybrid search features we rely on.
[19:20] Sam Ortiz: we generally match core features; if there's a gap we'll propose a workaround or roadmap item. we've done custom connectors for a few customers.
[19:48] Maya Patel: about throttling and rate limits — we need predictable throttling not surprising 429s.
[19:58] Priya Desai: Dedicated gives deterministic throughput, hosted has fair-use and quotas. we can set quotas per route and per token.
[20:20] Jordan Lee: how about client SDKs — we use a python sdk heavily and some go wrappers.
[20:30] Alex Kim: we have python, node, and go SDKs; they implement the parity layers. we'll share code snippets.
[20:50] Samir Gupta: on infra cost — if we use Dedicated, what's the minimum commit?
[21:00] Alex Kim: Dedicated contracts vary, typical starting commit is monthly reserved GPU pool; we'll include ballpark numbers in the follow-up.
[21:18] Maya Patel: can you demonstrate a sample POC run of 10k requests and show the dashboard?
[21:30] Priya Desai: I can show a recorded dashboard from a similar POC — loading now. (screen) here's request distribution, p50/p95, and cost breakdown. note the redwood optimize suggestions on batching gave ~22% cost reduction in that run.
[22:10] Jordan Lee: interesting. 22% is material. what's the confidence interval on that?
[22:20] Priya Desai: depends on traffic shape; we'll instrument your traces to refine the estimate.
[22:40] Chris Rivera: security — can you provide SOC2 docs and a sample DPA?
[22:52] Alex Kim: yes, security pack link will be shared; we'll add DPA and SSO configs.
[23:10] Maya Patel: can we get a quick run of a streaming summarization example with a long doc?
[23:22] Priya Desai: sure, I'll run a 4k token summarization. (run) streaming chunks appear, latency per chunk ~60ms p50. output matches our schema.
[24:05] Jordan Lee: looks good. a couple of users mentioned slight wording differences, but acceptable.
[24:18] Maya Patel: about rollout strategy — can Redwood do traffic mirroring so we can validate outputs without impacting prod?
[24:30] Sam Ortiz: yes, traffic mirroring and shadowing supported; you can run in parallel and compare metrics.
[24:50] Alex Kim: ok wrapping up the tech demo portion — high-level next steps: we'll send parity mapping doc, pricing, security pack, and propose POC dates.
[25:05] Jordan Lee: good. any blockers we should flag? security sign-off and performance on long contexts will be the main ones.
[25:18] Chris Rivera: correct, I'll own the security checklist.
[25:28] Alex Kim: noted — Chris you'll get the security pack and we can hop on a follow-up to go through it.
[25:40] Maya Patel: and I'll prepare the prompt suites and traces to share.
[25:50] Priya Desai: we'll draft the POC plan including sample scripts, target metrics, and instrumentation steps.
[26:10] Jordan Lee: thanks, one more question — do you offer assistance for model distillation or fine-tuning during migration?
[26:22] Priya Desai: we have partnerships and runbooks for fine-tuning and RLHF workflows; for now most customers start with parity and then iterate.
[26:40] Samir Gupta: on observability, does the console provide token-level cost attribution per route and per user?
[26:50] Priya Desai: yes token-level breakdowns, per-route dashboards, and you can tag keys to attribute to users.
[27:05] Jordan Lee: ok that answers most questions. can you send a proposed POC scope and dates?
[27:12] Alex Kim: yes we'll propose a 30-45 day POC, kickoff next week if that works for you.
[27:25] Jordan Lee: next week is tight but 2 weeks from now is fine.
[27:30] Alex Kim: perfect we'll circulate a few times.
[27:38] Priya Desai: quick note — a few transcriptions may have name typos, e.g., Together was read as "togeth-er" in one clip, ignore that.
[27:52] Maya Patel: ha, yeah transcripts are always fun.
[28:00] Alex Kim: ok final recap: action items Alex will send parity mapping + pricing; Priya will prepare POC config; Maya will share traces; Chris will send security checklist. We'll schedule POC kickoff and add Redwood SEs for onboarding.
[28:25] Jordan Lee: thanks everyone, appreciate the walkthrough.
[28:30] Alex Kim: thanks all — we'll follow up in email with links and the doc set.
[28:36] (call ends, remaining time was Q&A and scheduling — recording saved)

Notes: transcript contains occasional transcription errors and misnaming; original recording available on request.
